The reason is there are regional strains. If you get a flu shot in Nebraska, it's for a different strain than in Cali. If you travel or others travel, you don't nesc. have protection from the other strains.

Close, there are indeed hundreds of strains and they Can be regional (but not necessarily), but the main issue is that the vaccine is only designed to combat the top 3 PREDICTED strains for the following year. Those predictions can be way, WAY off (and have been), a new strain can emerge (or a really old one resurface after nearly a century), you simply lose the lotto and encounter a strain that's not in the vaccine, etc...

My wife was the go-to person for all Tamiflu calls a few years back (as in from hospitals, doctors, research facilities, the CDC, etc...), I now know way too fucking much about the flu.

Still important to get the shot every year though, it's called "Herd Immunity" ~ it's not about you, the individual, it's about society as a whole. You can be a carrier even if you never feel symptoms, and pass that on to someone who could die from it (either directly/first hand or through multiple retransmission's). There's nothing in that shit that "causes" anything, unless you have an egg allergy.
